title: Symmetry painting
examples: Teacher, what does it mean to be symmetrical?
Can we make a butterfly using symmetry?
How do I find the line of symmetry?

explain.say: Look at this picture. Do you see that line right down the middle?
A mirror pattern means that both sides look exactly the same.
We can make our own patterns by folding paper in half first.

items: Press and cut the other side

explain.say: When you fold paper, the crease line is your line of symmetry.
A butterfly has perfect symmetry when you fold it down the middle.
In real life, your face shows beautiful symmetry all the time.

faq.a: Symmetry means that one side of your artwork is a mirror image of the other side. You can also ask: Does it have to be perfect? Or: What does it mean to be balanced?
asks: How do I make something look balanced?

faq.q: Do I need a mirror to find symmetry?
faq.a: No, you can use a fold line to check if something is symmetrical. You might also ask: Can I use a piece of string? Or: Is a fold the same as a mirror?
asks: How do I check for symmetry?

faq.q: How do I use folding for art?
faq.a: You fold the paper and draw on one side, then cut or draw on the other side to match. You could also ask: What is 'fold and print'? Or: What do I do after I fold it?
asks: Can I draw on both sides?

faq.a: Many things in nature, like leaves and butterflies, show symmetry. However, some things are not perfectly symmetrical. You might ask: Are all animals symmetrical? Or: Does nature always follow rules?

faq.q: What if my drawing is not symmetrical?
faq.a: It is okay if it is not perfect; art can be messy and fun. You can try to make one side match the other side to practice. You might ask: Is it wrong if it's not perfect? Or: How do I fix it?
asks: What if I mess up the symmetry?
Can I still make art if it's not perfect?

facts: Symmetry means that two sides are like a mirror image.
When you fold paper, the crease line is the line of symmetry.
Butterflies and many leaves show natural symmetry.
You can create symmetrical art by folding paper in half.

quiz.say: If I draw a heart and fold it, the fold line is the line of:
quiz.why: The fold line acts like a mirror, making both halves match.

wrong.0: The center is just a point, not the line that divides the two equal sides.
wrong.1: The edge is the outside border, not the dividing line.
wrong.2: Color describes what you draw, not the shape's balance.

quiz.say: To make a pattern symmetrical, what must you do with the two sides?

options.show: be drawn on the same day
options.say: be drawn on the same day

quiz.why: Mirror images mean one side is exactly like the other side.

wrong.1: Different colors are fine, but they must still look the same shape.
wrong.2: The time you draw them has nothing to do with their balance.
wrong.3: The tools used do not change if the sides are balanced.

quiz.say: When using fold and print, what is the first step?
quiz.why: You must fold the paper first to create the line you will use for symmetry.

wrong.1: If you draw on both sides first, you won't know where the line of symmetry is.
wrong.2: Cutting comes after you have drawn your pattern on one side.
wrong.3: Color choice is not the first step; folding is.
